    GTRigidPhysics 1.0.0 — Rigid Body Physics for Minecraft

    GTRigidPhysics API Overview

    GTRigidPhysics is a rigid body physics engine for Minecraft Paper 26.2. Buildings collapse in whole sections according to a structural integrity analysis, and the debris falls and tumbles under real rigid body simulation. It also provides standalone physics objects: vehicles, mechanisms, dice, ragdolls and more. Server-side only — players do not need any client mod.

    This is the API reference for plugin developers. For installing the plugin, tuning its configuration, or understanding how each system works, see the documentation site. This page covers interfaces, parameters and contracts only.

    Where to start

    There is exactly one entry point: RigidPhysicsAPI. Obtain it via RigidPhysicsProvider.get(), from your own plugin's onEnable() — not onLoad(), where GTRigidPhysics has not been enabled yet.

    Sub-services are split by domain, each in its own subpackage of cn.gtedd.rigidphysics.api.*:

    Common sub-services
    What you want to doPackage
    Spawn, query and manipulate rigid bodiesapi.object
    Trigger or intercept structural collapseapi.collapse, api.structure
    Query and override per-block physics materialsapi.material
    Vehicles, mechanisms, characters, ragdollsapi.vehicle, api.mechanism, api.character, api.ragdoll
    Gravity and magnetic fieldsapi.field
    Player grabbing and raycast hitsapi.interaction
    Client-side effects such as camera rollapi.effect
    Listen to events (Bukkit events)api.event

    Three modules — pick by what you need

    Modules published to Maven
    ArtifactPurposeSize
    cn.gtedd:gtrigidphysics-api This is all most plugins need. Interfaces, events and value objects. Tens of KB, no native
    cn.gtedd:gtrigidphysics-common Pure logic: structural integrity analysis, cluster splitting, budget management, settle rules. No Bukkit dependency, unit-testable without a server. Small
    cn.gtedd:gtrigidphysics-physics The jolt-jni wrapper. Only needed if you drive the rigid body world directly. Tens of MB (native for three platforms)

    Declare the dependency as compileOnly, never implementation — the API is provided at runtime by the plugin installed on the server, and shading it into your own jar only causes class conflicts: 

    repositories {
    maven("https://gtedd.github.io/GTRigidPhysics/")
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly("cn.gtedd:gtrigidphysics-api:1.0.0")
}

    Three global constraints

    1. Main thread only. Unless a method's own documentation says otherwise, every method in this API must be called from the server main thread. Dispatching to the internal physics thread is the implementation's job; callers neither need to nor should do it themselves.
    2. Always null-check when obtaining the service. On an unsupported platform, or when the native library fails to load, the plugin disables itself and the interface is never registered. The plugin being installed does not mean the service is available.
    3. When physics is unavailable, calls fail silently rather than throwing. While RigidPhysicsAPI.isPhysicsAvailable() is false, spawn calls return null and force calls return 0. Check that method to tell "plugin not installed" apart from "installed but physics did not come up".

    License

    The api, common and physics modules are MIT licensed, so closed-source plugins may depend on them freely. The plugin itself (GTRigidPhysics-*.jar) is GPL-3.0. packetevents is a required dependency plugin and is not shaded in.
